newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel warns FDP about further attacks on his work.
newsitem.headline: Waigel warns FDP about further attacks on his work.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel warned on Friday against further attacks on his work by the Free Democratic Party, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's junior coalition partner.

Waigel, a top ally of Kohl, said in an interview with Bild Zeitung newspaper that the critical comments by top FDP officials about the rising budget deficit should be directed at the economics ministry and not him.
"When unemployment worsens more than what experts have predicted, that leads to a higher burden on the budget," Waigel said.
"And when the economics ministry has predicted economic growth to be too optimistic, then the FDP should accuse them and not me," he added.
Waigel said Kohl's coalition was not in danger of collapsing over the issue of Germany's budget deficits and whipping them into shape for European currency union.
He reaffirmed that the "solidarity surcharge" to pay for German unification would be lowered in 1998 but that the level of the reduction had not yet been finalised.
Waigel said on Wednesday that the 1997 budget deficit would not exceed the planned level of 56.5 billion marks despite lower tax revenues and higher unemployment payouts.
That would put Germany's deficit below the three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) required in the Maastricht Treaty for membership in currency union, slated to begin in January 1999.
Waigel said in the Bild interview that other measures would be found to keep the budget deficit below that level but he did not specify how it would be done.
